newsitem.title: UK: Mild downward pressure seen on BSkyB shares.
newsitem.headline: Mild downward pressure seen on BSkyB shares.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc were seen suffering from slight downward pressure after the satellite TV operator reported mildly disappointing subscriber growth, analysts said.
But BSkyB's first quarter results, which saw pre-tax profit rise 31 percent, were broadly in line with market expectations, they added. "There were no big surprises," commented one.
But subscriber growth of 146,000 in the three months to September came in about 8,000 lower than some industry watchers had forecast. "The subscriber growth is not exciting," said another analyst.

While studying the results statement, one analyst noted profit margins had gone down slightly as operating cost grew 26 percent against a revenue increase of 24 percent. "So, if people want to be negative there are a couple of things to hang onto, but there is nothing really negative," he added.

BSkyB said first-quarter subcriber growth only really took off in September. Comprehensive terrestrial coverage of the European soccer championship and the Atlanta Olympics held back growth earlier in the quarter, the satellite TV operator added.
BSkyB's first-quarter profit rose to 66.26 million stg from 50.77 million.
